_info: This template documents the shape of per-repo config files stored at {USER_AGENTS}/{repo_name}/.local-config.json. It is tracked in git so new installs know the expected structure. The live config files are NEVER in the repo — they live under the user-level framework directory.

_convention.rule: All local-only configuration lives under the user-level framework directory (~/.agents/ on Unix, %USERPROFILE%\.agents\ on Windows). Global identity and preferences are root-level files. Per-repo credentials and state live at {USER_AGENTS}/{repo_name}/.local-config.json.

user_level_structure.identity: {USER_AGENTS}/identity.json — author name and email, shared across all repos
user_level_structure.preferences: {USER_AGENTS}/preferences.json — framework version, update check state, global defaults
user_level_structure.framework_files: {USER_AGENTS}/directives/, standards/, skills/, workflows/ — installed from master repo, shared across all repos
user_level_structure.common_templates: {USER_AGENTS}/common/templates/ — ticket template, board template, reusable scaffolding
user_level_structure.per_repo_tickets: {USER_AGENTS}/{repo_name}/project/tickets/ — local ticket files, persist across branches and sessions
user_level_structure.per_repo_temp: {USER_AGENTS}/{repo_name}/temp/ — transient data, cleaned after workflows complete

_convention.repo_name_derivation: The {repo_name} is the basename of `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` — e.g. if the repo is at C:\repo\ClientA\salesforce-project, then repo_name is 'salesforce-project'.
_convention.how_to_add: 1. Add a new top-level key to this template with empty placeholder values. 2. Document the key in the skill's SKILL.md under 'Credential Loading' or 'Local Config'. 3. The install flow reads {USER_AGENTS}/{repo_name}/.local-config.json, detects blank fields under its key, and prompts the user only for what is missing. 4. Never create parallel local config files or directories.
_convention.naming: Use lowercase, short, descriptive key names (e.g. 'jira', 'slack', 'github'). Nest related fields one level deep. Do not nest deeper than two levels.
_convention.security: Keys that hold secrets (tokens, passwords, private keys) must be named clearly (e.g. 'api_token', 'secret'). The install flow must never echo secret values back to the user. The SKILL.md must document which fields are sensitive.
